subject: Business Models
title: Seeding Supply
description: A quick win: understand Seeding Supply.

hook.text: Reddit's founders created thousands of fake accounts to make the site look active at launch.

buildup.text: Seeding means creating initial supply yourself so the platform looks alive when real users arrive.

discovery.text: PayPal seeded eBay by buying and selling items to themselves—creating both supply and demand.

twist.text: Bumble seeded its dating app by recruiting sorority women on college campuses. Supply attracted demand.

climax.text: Seeding is the scrappy path: fake it until real supply arrives and takes over organically.

punchline.text: No supply? Create it yourself first. Every platform seeds.

quiz.question: How did PayPal seed its platform?
options: Buying and selling on eBay themselves

details.summary: Seeding supply is the strategy of bootstrapping a platform's supply side before demand arrives, solving the chicken-and-egg problem. Tactics include paying early suppliers, importing content, creating supply internally, or partnering with existing suppliers who bring their own audiences.
details.whyItMatters: Every platform faces the cold start problem: no users means no value. Seeding supply creates enough initial value to attract the first wave of demand, which then attracts organic supply in a self-sustaining cycle.
takeaways: Platforms must create initial supply value before demand users arrive
Common tactics include paying creators, importing content, and partnerships
The goal is reaching the tipping point where organic supply growth sustains itself

faq.question: What are proven strategies for seeding platform supply?
faq.answer: Reddit created fake accounts to populate early discussions. Uber guaranteed minimum earnings for early drivers. YouTube uploaded content and acquired creators. DoorDash manually added restaurant menus without asking first. Each approach bootstrapped supply before demand existed.

faq.question: How do you know when seeding supply has worked?
faq.answer: When organic supply begins growing without subsidies and retention rates for both sides exceed sustainability thresholds. The platform has achieved critical mass when removing seeded supply would not collapse the marketplace because organic activity sustains it.
